question: According to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways' annual report (2020-2021), which position does India have in terms of road networks in the world?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Second**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India has the second-largest road network in the world, as per the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways' annual report (2020-2021).
 
• The total length of the road network in India is over 5.89 million kilometers.
 
• The Indian road network comprises National Highways, State Highways, and other roads.
 
• This extensive network facilitates efficient transportation and connectivity throughout the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Highways:**

 
 
• National Highways are the primary roadways that connect major cities and regions across India.
 
• They are managed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
 
• National Highways constitute about 2% of the total road network but carry about 40% of the road traffic.
 
 
 
• **State Highways:**
 
 
• State Highways are roads that connect important cities within a state and link them with National Highways or highways of neighboring states.
 
• These highways are managed and maintained by the respective state governments.
 
 
 
• **Other Roads:**
 
 
• Other roads include district roads, rural roads, and urban roads that provide connectivity within districts, rural areas, and cities respectively.
 
• These roads are crucial for the last-mile connectivity and are maintained by local bodies such as Panchayats and Municipalities.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Road Network:**
 
 
• A well-developed road network is essential for economic growth, as it facilitates the movement of goods and people.
 
• It improves access to services such as healthcare and education, especially in rural areas.
 
• It also plays a critical role in national security by enabling the quick movement of defense forces and supplies.
